What is the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis code for this patient?

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: Not Specified
Medical Record Number: Not Specified
Date of Admission: Not Specified
Date of Discharge: Not Specified

INTRODUCTION:
The patient is an 81-year-old woman who visited the department of internal medicine in our hospital with complaints of loss of appetite, abdominal distension, and an upper abdominal mass. She had a history of left breast cancer 11 years ago. The patient was diagnosed with peritoneal metastasis of recurrent breast cancer and was put on endocrine therapy using letrozole.

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient's symptoms improved with endocrine therapy, and she showed recovery from pleural metastasis and pleural effusion. Tumor marker values fluctuated during the course of treatment, with no abnormal CEA values obtained, and CA15-3 and BCA225 values gradually declining from the time of recurrence and returning to normal levels 2 years later. NCC-ST-439 value gradually increased up to 49 U/ml 6 months later, with a gradual decline thereafter along with the other tumor markers. The patient was currently receiving treatment in the outpatient department and is still alive on the same medication.

DISCHARGE OUTCOME:
The patient is being discharged in stable condition with continued endocrine therapy.

FOLLOW-UP:
No relapse of malignancy has been detected after a period of 6 years.

ATTENDING PHYSICIAN:
Not Specified
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Letrozole.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
Continue endocrine therapy as prescribed. Follow up with your healthcare provider as recommended.

text:
# ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis: **C78.6 – Secondary malignant neoplasm of retroperitoneum and peritoneum**

**Why this code**

- The patient presented with loss of appetite, abdominal distension and an upper abdominal mass. Work-up showed **peritoneal metastasis from recurrent breast cancer**. That condition, found after study, caused the admission.
- In ICD-10-AM, cancer that recurs at a distant site, such as the peritoneum, is coded as a **secondary** neoplasm. It is not coded as a new primary.
- The neoplasm sequencing standard (ACS 0236) applies here. When the admission is for the metastatic site and its symptoms, the secondary neoplasm becomes the principal diagnosis.

**Likely additional codes**

- **C50.9** – Malignant neoplasm of breast, unspecified (left breast, quadrant not specified). Use this if the primary is considered still active, since disease has recurred. If the primary is documented as excised with no residual disease, use **Z85.3** (personal history of breast cancer) instead.
- **C78.2** – Secondary malignant neoplasm of pleura (pleural metastasis).
- **J91** – Malignant pleural effusion, if it was treated or relevant during the admission.

The final code assignment should be confirmed against the withheld discharge diagnosis section and your local coding standards.
